_metadata.description: Code Facts intake, per-workspace test planning, canonical framework detection, and the agent-readable maturity assessment.

requirements.title: Discover test surfaces through Code Facts
requirements.description: ValidateScenario calls Code Facts for surfaces and parse units, builds a normalized target model, and returns a degraded result with an explicit finding when Code Facts is unavailable rather than guessing from the filesystem.

validation.notes: Fake Code Facts client drives workspace discovery; unavailable discovery returns a degraded plan with a discovery finding.

requirements.title: Build a per-workspace test plan
requirements.description: The plan builder derives Go workspaces from Go parse units, TypeScript/Vite UI workspaces from TypeScript parse units plus package.json, and Python fallback workspaces with explicit unsupported-by-Code-Facts evidence, producing a dry-run plan in both human and JSON output.

validation.notes: Fixture parse-unit reports produce deterministic per-workspace plans including the degraded Python path.

requirements.title: Require canonical test frameworks
requirements.description: Each workspace is assigned its canonical framework (Go go test, React/Vite vitest, Python pytest preferred / unittest degraded). Jest in a React/Vite UI, a missing test script, a missing coverage config, and a package-manager mismatch each emit a stable finding.

validation.notes: Fixtures cover Vitest-ok, Jest-degraded, missing-script, missing-coverage-config, and pm-mismatch cases.

requirements.title: Emit an agent-readable maturity assessment
requirements.description: Responses include stable finding codes, evidence, remediation, recommended skills, current and next Unit Health local maturity, the blocking findings for the next level, and global semantic impact grouping; every emitted finding code maps in .vrooli/maturity.json.

validation.notes: Golden response asserts deterministic finding codes, current/next level transitions, and that every code has a maturity mapping.

requirements.title: Human output is the default, JSON is opt-in
requirements.description: `unit-health validate scenario <name>` renders a useful human report by default using the shared maturity renderer; `--json` emits the same assessment structurally for programmatic consumers.

validation.notes: CLI tests assert human output without --json and structural JSON parity with --json.
